stories.title: Woman claims her stepfather used Grok to transform childhood photo into explicit imagery
stories.simple_summary: Someone used an AI tool called Grok to turn an old childhood photo into explicit harmful images. This is a serious crime that harms children.
stories.why_it_matters: If you share family photos online, be aware that AI tools can misuse them in illegal ways. Be careful about what photos you post where.

stories.title: Have a laugh at AI’s expense by roleplaying as a chatbot
stories.simple_summary: A website lets people play a game where they pretend to be an AI chatbot and answer questions, while comparing their answers to what a real AI would say.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you — it's just a fun game people play on the internet.

stories.title: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new watermarks will work
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic (a company that makes AI) is explaining how they'll add invisible identification marks to content made by their AI, like a stamp that proves it's AI-made.
stories.why_it_matters: This might help people tell real photos and writing from AI-made ones, which could protect you from being fooled.

stories.title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition
stories.simple_summary: SpaceX, the rocket company, bought a smaller company called Cursor that helps programmers write code with AI assistance.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and tech workers — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Prediction: These 3 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stocks Will Rise More than 30% Before 2026 Is Over
stories.simple_summary: Someone is predicting that certain AI company stocks will go up in value by more than 30% by the end of 2025.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investment advice — mostly relevant only if you buy stock. There's no guarantee these predictions will happen.

stories.title: Google Opens the Gates of AI Slop Hell
stories.simple_summary: Google is releasing AI tools that generate text and images, and there's criticism about the quality or nature of what they produce.
stories.why_it_matters: Google is making more AI tools available, but the headline doesn't explain the actual issue clearly enough to know what it means.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an Instagzam
stories.simple_summary: Instagram changed its logo design this week — the way the word "Instagram" looks and appears has been redesigned.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect you at all — it's just a cosmetic change to how the Instagram app looks.

stories.title: You can now turn off Google Gemini’s visible watermarks
stories.simple_summary: Google is now letting you remove the visible sparkle watermark from images and videos your AI tools create.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google's AI tools to make images, you can now hide the mark that shows it's AI-made, though Google keeps invisible tracking marks for identification.

stories.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations
stories.simple_summary: Google will let people turn off the visible watermark on AI-generated files, though invisible identification marks will still be there.
stories.why_it_matters: Similar to the previous story — if you make images with Google's AI, you can now remove the visible watermark.

stories.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is ‘for everyone’?
stories.simple_summary: Mark Zuckerberg (who runs Meta/Facebook) released an AI tool that anyone can download and use themselves, saying AI should be available to everyone instead of just big companies.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're interested in AI tools, this means more options will become available to regular people instead of only big tech companies controlling them.

stories.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs
stories.simple_summary: A company called Kog says that computers designed for AI (GPUs) can handle a certain type of AI task better than people thought.
stories.why_it_matters: This is technical engineering news — mostly relevant to companies building AI systems, not to everyday users.

stories.title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
stories.simple_summary: Amazon and Google are making huge profits from their AI services, creating a pattern where they profit from selling AI tools and also profit from the demand those tools create.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching these companies — the news is about how profitable AI is for big tech giants.
